Chase Field Parking Guide: Garages, Rideshare & Drop-Off

Scottsdale Sprinters’ short answer on Chase Field parking: use the attached 1,500-car Chase Field Garage on 4th Street, which is first come, first served, or pre-book a nearby space through ParkWhiz, the Diamondbacks’ preferred parking partner, and carry a card and cash because some lots take only one. Rideshare pickups use 5th Street north of Washington Street or Jackson Street east of 9th Street, and light rail stops at 3rd Street and Washington or 3rd Street and Jefferson. For a group, one chauffeured vehicle replaces the garage, the payment and the drive out after the final out.

Last updated: September 24, 2026

Where do you park for Chase Field?

Chase Field has an attached 1,500-car garage just south of the ballpark on 4th Street that works first come, first served, and the Diamondbacks also offer pre-booked spaces through ParkWhiz, their preferred parking partner, so you can hold a spot before driving to the game. The ballpark is at 401 East Jefferson Street in downtown Phoenix, bounded by 7th Street on the east, 4th Street on the west, Jefferson Street on the north and the Southern Pacific Railroad tracks on the south. The Diamondbacks’ traffic advice is to park in the same quadrant you drive in from. Arriving from the south, for example, means parking between 3rd Avenue and 9th Street, from Lincoln Street to Jefferson Street. Payment is not the same everywhere. The Diamondbacks warn that some garages and lots around Chase Field take only credit cards while others take only cash, so carry both unless the space is prepaid. The City of Phoenix’s ParkPHX tool lists every public downtown parking facility in one place, with height limits, accessible spaces and reservations at participating facilities. Downtown parking is not one system. The City of Phoenix runs its own garages through the Phoenix Convention Center, and the Diamondbacks’ pre-booking runs through ParkWhiz, so rates and payment rules differ by facility. Book or choose the space before you leave, not at the last light before the ballpark.

What should you know about the Chase Field Garage?

The Chase Field Garage is attached to the ballpark just south of it on 4th Street, holds 1,500 cars, takes high-profile vehicles at every entrance, sets aside 31 accessible spaces, and has its own entrance on Level 3 for Suite and 200-level seats, with accessible turnstiles. All of its parking, the accessible spaces included, is first come, first served. When demand is high, the Diamondbacks say some garages accept only special parking passes, so a driver without one may need another garage. A sign at the booth shows when accessible parking in the Chase Field or Jefferson Street garage is full, before you pull in. The Jefferson Street Garage is the second garage the team names. Both garages have bicycle racks at street level, which the Diamondbacks list among the places to lock a bike, because bicycles are not allowed inside the ballpark. If the plan depends on the attached garage, pre-book or arrive early. The City of Phoenix, which runs the city-owned downtown garages, says spaces are in high demand during peak events.

Where is the Chase Field rideshare drop-off and pickup?

The Diamondbacks publish 2 rideshare points for pickup and drop-off, 5th Street north of Washington Street and Jackson Street east of 9th Street, plus a staffed drop-off on the south side of Jefferson Street just west of 7th Street, near Gate K, listed in the ballpark’s accessibility guide. One rideshare point is north of the ballpark, past Washington Street; the other is east of it, beyond 9th Street on Jackson Street. Pick the one on the side you are heading home from and agree on it before the game. A group that splits between the two points is waiting in two places. The Jefferson Street drop-off is staffed and has shaded benches for guests waiting on a ride. The driver who drops a guest there should ask for a Pick-Up Pass, which carries a map and directions back to the same spot after the game. Hold it up when traffic control detours you, so staff can direct you back to that lot. None of these points is reserved for chauffeured vehicles: the Diamondbacks publish no separate limo or charter zone. A booked vehicle works from the published points and the instruction confirmed for the booking. The team also warns that traffic around the ballpark can be rerouted as conditions dictate, as it does for southbound 3rd Street at Washington Street.

Can you take light rail to Chase Field?

Yes, Valley Metro’s A line stops at 2 stations near the ballpark, 3rd Street and Washington and 3rd Street and Jefferson, with trains every 15 to 20 minutes, and the Diamondbacks list 13 light rail Park-and-Ride locations for fans who drive part of the way. Buy the fare at any station with cash, credit or debit, or load the Valley Metro app or a Copper card before the game. The Diamondbacks suggest paying in advance to skip the lines after the game, and a daily fare cap means you stop paying once you reach it. Valley Metro also lists 2 bus connections for Chase Field: Route 1 on Washington Street and Route 7 on 7th Street. The Diamondbacks’ Park-and-Ride list runs from 19th Avenue and Dunlap to Gilbert Road and Main Street, and the Valley Metro app plans the trip from any of them. Rail suits a couple or a small party staying near a station. A larger group coming from Scottsdale resorts has more steps: getting everyone to a Park-and-Ride, onto one train and back again after the final out.

How much time and hassle does parking at Chase Field add?

Driving yourself adds 3 jobs to the game: getting a space before the garage or lot fills, paying the way that facility accepts, and leaving by the Diamondbacks’ quadrant exit routes after the final out, alongside everyone else leaving the ballpark at the same time. Arrival comes first. Gates open 90 minutes before first pitch Sunday through Friday and 2 hours before first pitch on Saturday, and the city says downtown garages are in high demand during peak events. Pre-booking through ParkWhiz or ParkPHX removes the search, not the drive. Then comes the exit. The Diamondbacks route traffic by quadrant after the game. From the southeast quadrant, south of Jefferson and east of 4th Street, drivers go south to Lincoln Street and then east to 7th Street. From the southwest quadrant they go south to Lincoln, which becomes Grant, and west to 7th Avenue. North of Washington, 3rd and 7th Avenues lead to the freeways. The drive in has its own warnings. From north central Phoenix the team calls 7th Street the least preferred route because of heavy use, and it calls the 3rd Street HOV exit the least preferred during arrival. None of it is hard, but all of it falls on whoever drives, who also has to stay fit to drive home.

Why does a chauffeured drop-off beat parking at Chase Field?

A chauffeured drop-off removes 3 costs of driving: the group steps out at the drop-off point confirmed for the booking instead of walking in from wherever a space was found, nobody sits in a garage exit line after the game, and one vehicle carries everyone, so nobody has to be the designated driver. It is not a way around traffic control. After the game every vehicle, ours included, moves with the downtown traffic plan, and the chauffeur meets the group at the agreed point once it is reachable. What changes is who does the work: the chauffeur handles the route in, the drop-off, the timing of the pickup and the route out. One vehicle also keeps a group together. Separate cars mean separate garages, separate exits and separate arrival times. A Sprinter or bus arrives with everyone at once, which matters when the plan includes dinner or a hotel pickup before first pitch. The trade-off is timing. A pickup runs on the traffic plan and the chauffeur’s approach, not on the minute you walk out, so agree on the pickup point in advance and message the chauffeur once the whole group is together.

Which vehicle fits a Chase Field group, and what does it cost?

Match the vehicle to the group: game-day friends start with the Ultra Luxury Party Sprinter or the Limo Party Sprinter (12-13 Pax), a client outing starts with the Executive Black Sprinter or the Executive White Sprinter, and a group larger than 28 moves up to the Executive Mini Coach (29 Pax) or the 56-Passenger Motorcoach. Seats come from the published fleet. For game-day groups: Ultra Luxury Party Sprinter up to 15, Limo Party Sprinter (12-13 Pax) up to 13, Limo Party Sprinter (16 Pax) up to 16 and Party Bus (28 Pax) up to 28. For client outings: Executive Black Sprinter up to 14, Executive White Sprinter up to 14, Maybach Jet Sprinter up to 9 and Mini Bus (24 Pax) up to 24. For more than 28 riders: Executive Mini Coach (29 Pax) up to 29 and 56-Passenger Motorcoach up to 56. Every rate prices the whole vehicle by the hour, and here is a 5-hour booking in each lead vehicle. The Ultra Luxury Party Sprinter is $250 an hour with a 4-hour minimum, so 5 billed hours come to $1,250 before tax, about $83 each when all 15 seats are filled. The Executive Black Sprinter is $145 an hour with a 4-hour minimum, so 5 billed hours come to $725 before tax, about $52 each when all 14 seats are filled. The Executive Mini Coach (29 Pax) is $225 an hour with a 4-hour minimum, so 5 billed hours come to $1,125 before tax, about $39 each when all 29 seats are filled. Those figures are arithmetic from the published rates, not a quote. An hourly booking keeps the vehicle for the whole outing, so the drive each way counts toward the hours. A ride there and a separate ride back can be booked as a transfer instead of by the hour; the written quote shows how the drive is priced.

How should a group plan the Chase Field arrival and pickup?

Plan 4 things before leaving the hotel: an arrival inside the gate window, which opens 90 minutes before first pitch Sunday through Friday and 2 hours before on Saturday, one agreed pickup point, one person who messages the chauffeur, and bags that pass the clear bag policy. The clear bag policy decides what leaves the vehicle. It allows one clear bag up to 12 by 6 by 12 inches or a one-gallon clear bag, plus a small clutch up to 4.5 by 6.5 inches, and no backpacks. A group that is dropped off has no car in the garage to leave a bag in, so settle bags at the hotel. The Diamondbacks’ locker partner, Mobile Locker Company, stores non-approved bags for a fee. For the return, choose the rideshare point on the side you will leave from, or the Jefferson Street drop-off when a guest needs the accessible entrance, and share it with the whole group before first pitch. When the game ends, gather first, then message the chauffeur once with the group count, rather than having several people send pins. Guests who have difficulty walking to their seats can ask any Chase Field staff member for a complimentary wheelchair escort from the gates or drop-off areas to their seats; the Diamondbacks say no advance request is needed. For a change of plan on the day, call the reservations team at (623) 986-6339 or email reservations@scottsdalesprinters.com.

When are the D-backs home games and concerts at Chase Field?

The Arizona Diamondbacks play 81 home games at Chase Field in 2027, from the home opener against the Marlins on Friday, April 2, 2027 to the last home game against the Dodgers on Sunday, September 26, 2027, and the team has not announced first-pitch times yet. The home stands, in order: April 2–7 (Marlins and Dodgers); April 16–21 (Padres and Cubs); April 30 – May 9 (Guardians, Orioles and Rangers); May 17–23 (Mariners and Rockies); May 31 – June 6 (Reds and Giants); June 14–20 (Braves and Red Sox); June 28 – July 4 (Mets and Giants); July 16–21 (Rockies and Cardinals); August 2–8 (Rays and Astros); August 12–15 (Brewers); August 23–29 (Nationals and Phillies); September 6–12 (Pirates and Royals); September 21–26 (Padres and Dodgers). Opening Day, Thursday, March 25, 2027, is on the road in San Diego, so the first game at Chase Field is the home opener. The Diamondbacks announce first-pitch times closer to the season, and they are added here as they are. Gates open 90 minutes before first pitch Sunday through Friday and 2 hours before first pitch on Saturday, so give the reservations team your game date when you book and the chauffeur plans the pickup around it. The one concert the Diamondbacks list for Chase Field as of September 24, 2026 is the Hondo Rodeo Fest, November 13–15, 2026: each night a full rodeo, then a full-length concert, with Tim McGraw and Miranda Lambert on Friday, Blake Shelton and Turnpike Troubadours on Saturday, and Parker McCollum and Lynyrd Skynyrd on Sunday. Shows for 2027 are announced by the ballpark closer to the date. One caveat for the season: Major League Baseball’s labor agreement expires on December 1, 2026. If a new agreement is not in place in time, games can move, and this list follows the official schedule as MLB and the Diamondbacks publish it.

Frequently asked questions

How much is parking at Chase Field?

The Diamondbacks do not publish one parking price. Garages and lots around the ballpark set their own rates, and some take only cards while others take only cash. To see a price before you go, pre-book through ParkWhiz, the team’s preferred parking partner, or compare downtown garages on the City of Phoenix’s ParkPHX.

Where is the best place to park for Chase Field?

The Chase Field Garage is attached to the ballpark, just south of it on 4th Street, with 1,500 spaces on a first come, first served basis. Otherwise the Diamondbacks advise parking in the same quadrant you drive in from, and pre-booking through ParkWhiz holds a space before you leave.

Is there free parking near Chase Field?

The Diamondbacks publish no free parking. Their alternative to a garage is light rail: they list 13 Park-and-Ride locations, and trains stop at 3rd Street and Washington or 3rd Street and Jefferson, within walking distance of the ballpark.

Where is the rideshare pickup at Chase Field?

At 5th Street north of Washington Street, or Jackson Street east of 9th Street. Agree on one with your group before the game.

Where is accessible parking and drop-off at Chase Field?

The attached garage has 31 spaces for a valid disabled plate or placard, first come, first served. The staffed drop-off is on the south side of Jefferson Street, just west of 7th Street, near Gate K. Ask for a Pick-Up Pass to get back to it after the game.

What time do Chase Field gates open?

90 minutes before first pitch Sunday through Friday, and 2 hours before first pitch on Saturday. The Diamondbacks post special gate times for some dates in their A-to-Z guide.

Can a chauffeured Sprinter drop our group at Chase Field?

Yes, at a point the live traffic plan allows. The Diamondbacks publish two rideshare points and a staffed drop-off on Jefferson Street but no separate limo or charter zone, so the chauffeur confirms the drop-off for your booking and vehicle.
